definitions.explanation: Describes something that causes fear or is frightening. Can also describe the feeling of being scared.

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{怖|こわ}かった⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
⟦{暗|くら}い→暗い：00647_kurai⟧⟦ところ→所：01137_tokoro⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{怖|こわ}い⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
{怖|こわ}い⟦{夢|ゆめ}→夢：01519_yume⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}ました→見る：00283_miru⟧。
⟦{犬|いぬ}→犬：00632_inu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{怖|こわ}くて、⟦{近|ちか}づけません→近づく：01958_chikazuku⟧。
examples.english: I'm scared of dogs, so I can't go near them.
When I was a child, I was scared of going outside alone at night.

notes:
{怖|こわ}い covers both "scary" (describing what causes fear) and "scared" (describing the feeling); context decides which. The feared thing is marked with ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧: ⟦{犬|いぬ}→犬：00632_inu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{怖|こわ}い ("I'm afraid of dogs").

USAGE:
- Use it of frightening things (a movie, a dog, the dark) and of one's own fear alike.
- For someone else's fear as an ongoing action, switch to the verb ⟦{怖|こわ}がる→怖がる：07574_kowagaru⟧ ("to be/act afraid"), since a plain adjective most naturally describes the speaker's own feeling.

REGISTER:
Neutral and everyday. The slangy ⟦ビビる→びびる：09292_bibiru⟧ ("to be freaked out") is casual only.

FORMS:
- {怖|こわ}くて: "scary and…" or "because it's scary"
- {怖|こわ}く⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧: "not scary"
- {怖|こわ}かった: "was scary"

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {怖|こわ}い⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧: scary story, ghost story
- {怖|こわ}い⟦{夢|ゆめ}→夢：01519_yume⟧: nightmare
- {怖|こわ}くて⟦{仕方|しかた}→仕方：01603_shikata⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧: to be terrified
- {怖|こわ}い⟦もの→物：02259_mono⟧⟦{知|し}らず→知る：00458_shiru⟧: fearless

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{恐|おそ}ろしい→恐ろしい：02338_osoroshii⟧: terrifying (stronger, more literary)
- ⟦{気味|きみ}が{悪|わる}い→気味悪い：10642_kimiwarui⟧: creepy, eerie
